original_question: Is the map H∗ (BPL(M )δ ; Fp ) → H∗ (BPL(M ); Fp ) an isomorphism in all degrees?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting §9.2, Question 9.10, which asks for the PL-homeomorphism analogue of Milnor’s conjecture: whether the homology comparison map H_*(BPL(M)^δ; F_p) -> H_*(BPL(M); F_p) is an isomorphism in all degrees. The same paragraph says this is motivated by Milnor’s conjecture for finite-dimensional Lie groups, and the sentence after Question 9.10 notes that Greenberg’s work implies the statement for PL_c(R). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: You correctly identified the ambient comparison between BPL(M)^δ and BPL(M), kept the mod-p coefficient field F_p, and preserved the exact qualitative claim that the map should be an isomorphism in all degrees. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks about homology H_*(-; F_p), not cohomology H^*(-; F_p). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
M should be identified as a PL manifold; that is the standing ambient object in §9.2. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The notation δ means that the same group PL(M) is equipped with the discrete topology, so BPL(M)^δ means B(PL(M)^δ). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The map should be made explicit as the natural comparison map induced by the identity homomorphism PL(M)^δ -> PL(M); this is implicit from the Milnor-conjecture analogy immediately before Question 9.10. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The coefficient field should be spelled out as F_p, the finite field with p elements, with p a prime. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

For a stand-alone formulation, 'in all degrees' should be made explicit as every homological degree * >= 0. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper does not replace PL(M) by PL_0(M) in Question 9.10, even though earlier questions in the subsection do use PL_0(M); keeping PL(M) is part of staying faithful to the paper’s wording. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a PL manifold M and a prime p. Let PL(M)^δ denote the group of PL homeomorphisms of M equipped with the discrete topology, and let BPL(M)^δ -> BPL(M) be the map induced by the identity homomorphism PL(M)^δ -> PL(M). Is the induced map on homology H_*(BPL(M)^δ; F_p) -> H_*(BPL(M); F_p) an isomorphism in every degree * >= 0? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly points to Question 9.10 in §9.2 because it matches the same pair of classifying spaces, the same coefficient field, and the same 'isomorphism in all degrees' formulation. The crucial correction is that the paper’s statement is in homology, not cohomology. The surrounding text in §9.2 provides the PL-manifold context and frames the question as the PL analogue of Milnor’s conjecture; the paper also records the special case PL_c(R). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
